context: Isaac, 2026-11-04: abilities and techniques no longer reflect the writing or the worldbuilding; he wants them more like One Piece, with names like 'World Cutting Slice' and 'Unlimited Works of Fate'.

batch1.north_star: One Piece, mythic at top: most fighters get one wild concept and loud named moves; the very top goes mythic.
batch1.scene_vs_card: Scene wins, card updates: anything on the page in an archived scene is written back to the card at scene end.
batch1.physics_place: After the spectacle: name, hit, awe first; the explanation comes right after, from a mouth or narration, and stays complete.

batch2.name_form: Loud for most, Art: Move on top: ordinary fighters get one big phrase; signature arts get a title with named moves under it.
batch2.language: Their culture's, glossed once: the fighter calls in their own tongue and the meaning lands in the same beat through narration or a witness.
batch2.big_words: Anyone, but the world reacts: a nobody can call his punch World-Ender; the room laughs until it works, and living up to it becomes part of the story.
batch2.who_names: A mix, and names can change: fighters, schools and witnesses all name things, and the most famous name wins out.

batch3.numbered_forms: Art picks its own count: numbering is optional, each art uses its own word for tiers (Acts, Entries, Verses, Knots), so the count becomes a threat.
batch3.epithets: Yes, and the world uses them: every major fighter has a title that travels ahead of them through crowds, newspapers, bounties and rumor; some are wrong or unflattering.
batch3.library_names: Rename and rewrite them all: keep each page's idea, give it a name with swagger and a short new entry; the old name survives as a scholar's term on the page.
batch3.comic_names: Anywhere the character earns it: goofy names can be truly lethal at any Stage on anyone whose card fits; cold killers and carded Moto stay serious.

batch4.kit_shape: One wild concept, many moves: one idea you can explain in a breath, then a growing list of named things done with it.
batch4.move_count: A few, growing in play: start with 3 to 5 and add one whenever a fight or scene earns it; the list records their story.
batch4.one_line_hook: Yes, plain enough for a kid: one sentence with no system words; if it can't be said simply the idea isn't ready.
batch4.weirdness: Anything, if it's fully explored: soup, debt, doors, boredom; any idea works if the character pushes it to a terrifying place.

batch5.system_link: Concept first, Wellspring after: dream up the idea first, then find the Wellspring and glyph that explain it; the system supports the idea without limiting it.
batch5.trait_domain_release: All one concept, escalating: keep all three; Trait is the idea, Release transforms the body, Domain makes the world obey it.
batch5.shared_arts: Yes, loud names by culture: famous arts everybody knows and argues about, each culture with its own name.

batch6.entry_shape: Hook, moves, then how it works: the fun reads first in seconds; the full mechanism lives below it for fights and anyone who wants it.
batch6.figures_place: A stat block at the bottom: each ability's numbers sit together at the end of the entry or card.
batch6.cost_counter_lines: One line each, on every art: they stay for fair fights but short and punchy; individual moves can skip them.
batch6.cost_feel: A price that fits the concept: keep reserve and body tells; big arts also carry a strange personal price from their own idea.

batch7.explanation_depth: Scale by size, always clear: a small move gets a line; a signature's first use or a finisher gets the full account after the hit; nobody is left confused.
batch7.calling_on_page: Volume set by character: showmen shout in capitals on their own line; killers and legends may whisper it.
batch7.ultimate_moment: Rare and staged: a big moment can get its own section title, a slowed run-up and the whole world reacting; it costs enough to stay rare.

batch8.new_moves: Natalie invents, your PC stays yours: NPCs can create and name new moves mid-fight, canon on use; for his PC she offers names and he keeps or cuts them.
batch8.move_upgrades: New name marks the jump: the move grows into a bigger name while the old one stays in use.
batch8.team_combos: Yes, and they're earned: crews and Resonant Pairs get named combos once a bond is real, and bicker about what to call them.
batch8.destruction_scale: Geography changes at the top: walls, then streets, then rivers and mountains; top-tier fights leave scars on the map the world names and remembers.

batch9.public_fame: Broadsheets, bounties, betting: papers print rankings and wanted bills, bookies take odds; fame changes prices, doors and who comes for you.
batch9.legendary_arts: Yes, a known and feared list: children know the names, scholars argue, people kill for them; some banned or lost, a few holders alive.
batch9.schools: Loud names, famous rivalries: schools are like football clubs, with colors, songs, grudges and a recognizable signature style.
batch9.named_gear: Named, famous, with histories: top pieces have names, reputations and past owners the public knows, on the existing Tier ladder.

batch10.everyday_powers: Everywhere and petty: streets are full of tiny, silly, useful arts; big powers feel bigger by comparison.
batch10.magitech_moves: Yes, tinkerers show off: inventors and operators shout model names and brag about patents; machines misfire in funny and terrible ways.
batch10.regional_styles: Yes, known at a glance: each place has signature moves, naming habits, costumes and jokes about the others.

batch11.system_words: Street words, scholars use terms: ordinary fighters use vivid local slang; Measurewrights, Guild people and analysts use the real terms.
batch11.wild_places: Big hook, still lived-in: major places get a premise you can say in one breath, with real rent, food and politics underneath.
batch11.villain_arts: Themed sets, personal cruelty: each villain group has a shared motif; each member's concept shows what they believe and did.
batch11.wiki_voice: Fun first, scholar's asides: keep the in-world narrator, open each page with spectacle and famous stories; technical detail follows.

batch12.pilot: Pilot three cards first: Muken, Raizan and one lower-Stage fighter, plus a short sample fight, then the rest of Volume I, the 57 library pages and the wiki magic pages.
batch12.rewrite_freedom: Keep what happened, rethink the rest: anything shown in an archived scene stays true; each kit gets one concept and new names; unused pieces can be merged or cut; he can strike any of it.
batch12.old_scenes: Scenes stay, old names are history: archived scenes aren't edited; a renamed move's old name becomes what people once called it, and the card lists both.
batch12.other_creators: Hands off, offer the format: their cards stay untouched and they may use the new format if they choose.

batch13.darkness: Loud fun, real blood: the dark shonen rule stands; goofy names and color, while wounds, deaths and cruelty still land in full at turning points.
batch13.prose_model: Literary prose, loud moves: narration stays rich and thoughtful; shouted names and spectacle crash through it; The Weak Grade remains the model.
batch13.law_timing: Now, and adjust after the pilot: write the rules as R82 and update Natalie and the pipelines now; the pilot can still change them.
batch13.reopen: No, those are my calls: all 52 answers stand.
